extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, marketers, and communicators who write and distribute press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for crafting and distributing press releases to maximize readership and media pickup, focusing on headlines, body length, and send timing. Aimed at communicators seeking higher visibility and engagement for announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Less is More (Headlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the character length to 88 characters or less, and include the most important keywords in the first 55 to 70 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft concise, relevant headlines that search engines and readers will immediately recognize. Prioritize brevity and front-load key terms so they appear within the first 55–70 characters for visibility and SEO; total headline length should not exceed 88 characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with Why (Content Length)
rubrics_metrics.description: The longer the press release, the less likely the reader is to read it in its entirety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for approximately 600 words and prioritize leading with compelling reasons your audience should care about your announcement. Put the most important information up front (the 'why') to capture and retain reader attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing is Everything (Distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than sending at peak times when 52% of news is sent on the hour and half hour—particularly Tuesdays at 8:00 AM ET—choose unconventional send times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid busy, predictable send windows (e.g., on the hour/half hour and common slots like Tuesday 8:00 AM ET) to distinguish your release from competitors; consider unconventional times such as 8:47 AM to increase the chance your release stands out to journalists and audiences.
